title: Absorb the factor (9 p^2)^g by the same gate (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Under the #4484 gate `p ≥ max(64, 4K + 2C)` and `16 g ceil(log2 p) ≤ p`,

```text
g (9 p^2)^g exp(K p - p^2) < 2^{-C p}
```

for integers `p ≥ 2`, `g ≥ 1`, `K ≥ 0` and `C ≥ 0`. Four bits still suffice because `9 < 16`, so the exponent remains `L + 4 g + 2 g L + 2 K p - p^2`, and that exponent is at most `-C p - 1`.

Three bits are not a majorant of this shape. Since `9 > 8`, `(9 p^2)^g > 2^{3 g} p^{2 g}`. At the legal point `p = 128`, `g = 1`, the exponent written with `3` in place of `4` is negative, and `9 p^2 > 8 p^2`, so that negativity is not an upper bound.

The per-axis ceiling `9 p^2` stays a hypothesis. At `g = p^2` the substituted error is still greater than 1. No new κ. The selected record remains `23/10000`.

This answers the open question of #4493. It does not replay #4484 or #4493. The telescoping factor `p^6` is left open.
